description: Generate, wrap, validate and build Bonita custom pages — six supported frameworks (React, Vue, Angular, Svelte 5, SolidJS, Qwik). The toolkit at github.com/bonitasoft-ps/bonita-custom-page-toolkit includes runnable examples, framework skills with deployment rules, and a multilingual deployment guide for Bonita 2025.x. Tools call the same functions the standalone bonita-page CLI uses — single source of truth.

tools.name: scaffold_custom_page
tools.title: Scaffold a new Bonita custom page project
tools.description:
Create a NEW Bonita custom page project from one of the six framework templates. Use when the user explicitly says 'create a new app/page', 'scaffold a project', or doesn't have an existing codebase. The result is a complete project on disk with src/, page.properties, build scripts and multilingual deploy docs — ready to `npm install && npm run dist`.

— Use BEFORE calling this tool: ASK the user for `name`, `appToken`, and which framework (don't assume). Optionally ask `displayName`, `pageToken` (default 'home'), and `targetDir`. See the bonita-custom-page skill §Questions to ask.

— Don't use this when the user has an EXISTING SPA — call `wrap_existing_app` instead.

— After this tool succeeds: tell the user to `cd` into the project directory and run `npm run dist` (or `./build.sh`). The output JSON's `nextSteps` field gives the exact commands.

framework.description: Frontend framework. If unsure between options, recommend based on team familiarity (React/Vue/Angular for established teams) or COMPARISON.md (Svelte for smallest bundle with simple syntax, Solid for max performance, Qwik only when first-paint speed dominates).

name.description: Internal page name in camelCase. Becomes 'custompage_<name>' in page.properties and 'page-<name>.zip' as the output filename. Example: 'invoiceDashboard'.

displayName.description: Label shown in Bonita admin (e.g. 'Invoice Dashboard'). Free text. Defaults to `name` if omitted.

appToken.description: Bonita Application token in camelCase. The page will be served at /bonita/apps/{appToken}/{pageToken}/. The user creates this Application separately in Bonita admin (superAdminAppBonita/application-list/).

pageToken.description: Page token within the Application. Default 'home'. Becomes the second URL segment.

targetDir.description: Absolute path where the project should be created. Default: ./<name> from the current working directory. Must NOT exist.

tools.name: wrap_existing_app
tools.title: Wrap an existing SPA project into a Bonita custom page
tools.description:
Take an EXISTING React/Vue/Angular/Svelte/Solid/Qwik project (the user already has it on disk) and ADD the Bonita custom-page layer ON TOP, without modifying their `src/` code:

  - Adds `page.properties` at the project root
  - Adds `scripts/package-bonita.js` and `scripts/copy-docs.js`
  - Adds `docs/DEPLOY-README.{md,html}` (multilingual EN/FR/ES)
  - Adds `build.sh` + `build.bat`
  - Adds `dist` and `build:bonita` scripts to `package.json`
  - Adds `archiver` (and `cross-env` for Angular) as devDependencies

It also VERIFIES key configurations and emits WARNINGS (not failures) if it finds:
  - Vite `base` not `'./'`
  - Angular `baseHref` not `'./'`
  - Browser routing instead of hash routing
  - Missing `withCredentials` etc.

— Use BEFORE calling this tool: confirm the user has a project directory and ASK for `name` and `appToken`. Framework is auto-detected from package.json/angular.json.

— Don't use this when the user wants a NEW project — call `scaffold_custom_page` instead.

— After this tool succeeds: REVIEW the `warnings` array with the user. Each warning describes a config that the wrapper didn't auto-fix (because it doesn't touch their source code). The matching framework skill (e.g. bonita-react-app) has the fix for each warning.

framework.description: If omitted, auto-detected from package.json (react/vue/svelte/solid-js/@builder.io/qwik) or angular.json. Pass explicitly only if detection fails.

targetDir.description: Absolute path of the EXISTING project to wrap. Must contain a package.json (or angular.json for Angular).

name.description: Internal page name in camelCase. Becomes 'custompage_<name>'.

displayName.description: Label shown in Bonita admin. Defaults to `name`.

tools.name: validate_custom_page_zip
tools.title: Validate a custom-page ZIP before uploading to Bonita
tools.description:
Open a ZIP file and verify it has the exact layout Bonita requires:
  - `page.properties` AT THE ZIP ROOT with `name=custompage_*` and `contentType=page|layout|theme|apiExtension|form`
  - `resources/` directory with `resources/index.html` inside

Returns a JSON report with `valid: true|false` and a list of `issues`. Use BEFORE the user uploads the ZIP to Bonita to catch packaging mistakes early — the most common one is `page.properties` accidentally placed under `resources/` instead of at the root.

— Use this when: the user has just built a ZIP and is about to upload, or wants to debug 'failed to import' errors in Bonita.
— Don't use for: validating page.properties content rules (this tool only checks ZIP structure + the bare minimum of page.properties fields).

zipPath.description: Absolute path to a page-*.zip file produced by `npm run dist` or `npm run build:bonita`.

tools.name: build_custom_page
tools.title: Build a custom-page project (npm install + dist)
tools.description:
Convenience wrapper. Run `npm install` (if `node_modules` is missing) and then the project's best available build script — in priority order: `dist` > `build:bonita` > `build`. Returns paths to the produced ZIP and the multilingual DEPLOY-README docs.

— Use this when the user wants to (re)build a project they already have set up.
— Don't use this for the FIRST setup of a project — call `scaffold_custom_page` (new) or `wrap_existing_app` (existing) first.

— After this tool succeeds: the user can call `validate_custom_page_zip` on the produced ZIP, or upload it to Bonita per the framework skill's deployment quick-reference.

projectDir.description: Absolute path to a Bonita custom-page project (must have package.json and at least one of: `dist`, `build:bonita`, `build` scripts).

tools.name: get_deployment_guide
tools.title: Return the Bonita deployment guide
tools.description:
Return the full step-by-step deployment guide for a given Bonita version, as Markdown. Use when the user asks 'how do I deploy this to Bonita?' or hits an issue uploading a ZIP.

Guides differ MEANINGFULLY between versions:
  - Bonita 2025.x: admin UI lives in TWO Living Applications (`superAdminAppBonita` and `adminAppEEBonita`). The legacy Portal admin UI (`/bonita/portal/admin`) is GONE.
  - Bonita 7.x: legacy Portal — Resources → Pages → Add.

Default to '2025.x' unless the user explicitly says they're on 7.x or earlier.

version.description: Bonita version. Default '2025.x' (current). For older deployments use '7.x'.

tools.name: list_custom_page_examples
tools.title: List the bundled custom-page examples
tools.description:
Return the catalog of example projects shipped with the toolkit. Each example is a complete runnable project (login + Bonita session probe + tasks list + logout) in one of the six supported frameworks. Use this when the user wants to:
  - See a working starting point before scaffolding their own
  - Compare frameworks (also see COMPARISON.md for measured metrics)
  - Copy an example as a template manually

The directory-bonita variants are turnkey deployments to specific Bonita Applications; the task-viewer variants are generic. All can be opened, customised and rebuilt independently.
